_note: ForgeMiner 1.8.8 (Oct 14): official GitHub release; its SHA-256 matches both the release notes and GitHub's own asset digest (checked Oct 16; the exe path was read from the zip's index). Moved up from 1.8.4 (verified live on the user's RTX 4070 SUPER on Oct 4, SHA c61474c1...de1b; still matches GitHub, so rolling back is one edit) for public-release fixes: 8 GB cards (3060 Ti, 3070, 2060 SUPER) no longer drop to a slower profile or send only rejected shares (1.8.5), RTX 30 no longer stops with CUDA error 700 (1.8.6), Pearl about +2% on RTX 40 at -12% board power (1.8.7), dead pool connections noticed in seconds (1.8.7). Defender check of 1.8.8 and a live share still to confirm (the app downloads and verifies it on Start). Closed source; the app only downloads the official release URL with its pinned SHA-256, never a rehosted copy (user, Oct 4: no need to ask the developer). Flags confirmed by a live run on Kryptex (Oct 4, 1.8.4): 122.9 TH/s at 196 W, share accepted. {tempLimit}/{tempResume} come from the app's settings (default 83/75 C: 80 would cycle on a normal gaming card); the miner pauses a hot card itself and the app only steps in 4 C above. powerArgs: ForgeMiner's --plimit is in watts and needs Administrator on Windows; the app runs without admin, so the cap only applies when the user runs it elevated (the miner keeps mining either way, to be confirmed live). devFee is per algorithm (%). BzMiner v100.45 (Oct 4): official GitHub release, SHA-256 matches GitHub's digest, not flagged by Defender on download or unpack (WildRig 0.51.3 was: Trojan:Script/CoinMiner!rfn). Used for Quantus on AMD and Intel Arc. Not yet run: its dev fee is only printed at startup, and --devices numbering and --set http_port need a live check on an AMD PC.
